must_identify.item: The failing requests come from the pod of a separate Deployment shop-api, which shares the app=api label and is therefore an endpoint of the api Service
must_identify.evidence: The api Service selects backends purely on `app=api` [6], and its endpoint list included three pods instead of the expected two: 10.244.1.148 and 10.244.2.137 from the legitimate `api` Deployment (2 replicas, created 21:01:01) [11, 13], plus 10.244.2.140 from a separate, unrelated `shop-api` Deployment (1 replica, created 21:01:09, 8 seconds later) [16].

must_identify.item: That pod returns 500 because its config lacks DATABASE_URL (KeyError), while the real api pods are healthy
must_identify.evidence: That pod runs a different codebase (`/code/app.py`) which throws `KeyError: 'DATABASE_URL'` on every `/items` request because the `shop-api` Deployment spec never sets a `DATABASE_URL` environment variable [14]. ... The two legitimate `api-f64486c4c-*` pods served 200 responses for every `/items` request logged in the same window, confirming they are healthy and not contributing to the error rate [9, 10, 12].

notes: The RCA identifies the root cause precisely and explicitly rules out redis, but it recommends no remediation. A reviewer may want to confirm that deleting, scaling down or relabeling shop-api would have been the intended action.

reviewer_ai.notes: Agree with the judge. The endpoints list (three IPs including 10.244.2.140), the shop-api pod labels (app=api), the KeyError: 'DATABASE_URL' 500s in its logs and the all-200 logs of the two real api pods all appear in the tool output. The RCA says kube-proxy 'round-robins' across endpoints; that is loose wording, since the default iptables mode picks endpoints at random, but it does not change the 1-in-3 conclusion. No fix is proposed.

fix_from_suggestions.reason: Scaling shop-api to zero and removing its app=api label are both listed acceptable fixes, and either one removes the broken DATABASE_URL-less pod from the api Service's endpoints.
